problem_text:
Поверхность правильного тетраэдра с длиной ребра \(239\) требуется полностью покрыть прямоугольными полосками размера \(1\times23\). Полоски можно накладывать друг на друга, сгибать вдоль рёбер тетраэдра и произвольно располагать на поверхности, однако резать или рвать их нельзя.

Найдите минимальное количество полосок, необходимое для покрытия всей поверхности тетраэдра.

problem.title: Мумифицированный тетраэдр
problem.statement:
Поверхность правильного тетраэдра с длиной ребра \(239\) требуется полностью покрыть прямоугольными полосками размера \(1\times23\). Полоски можно накладывать друг на друга, сгибать вдоль рёбер тетраэдра и произвольно располагать на поверхности, однако резать или рвать их нельзя.

Найдите минимальное количество полосок, необходимое для покрытия всей поверхности тетраэдра.
problem.solution:
Обозначим искомое число полосок через \(N\).

**Нижняя оценка.** Площадь поверхности правильного тетраэдра со стороной \(239\) равна
\[
4\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot239^2=239^2\sqrt3,
\]
а площадь каждой полоски равна \(23\). Так как полоски должны покрыть поверхность без пропусков, необходимо
\[
N\ge\left\lceil\frac{239^2\sqrt3}{23}\right\rceil=4302.
\]

**Верхняя оценка.** Разрежем поверхность тетраэдра по двум противоположным рёбрам — она развернётся в цилиндрическое кольцо высотой
\[
\frac{239\sqrt3}{2}
\]
и с длиной окружности
\[
2\cdot239=478.
\]

Разобьём это кольцо на \(478\) вертикальных полос шириной \(1\). Каждую такую полосу можно покрыть полосками \(1\times23\), уложенными вертикально. Их потребуется
\[
\left\lceil\frac{239\sqrt3}{46}\right\rceil=\lceil8.9991335437\ldots\rceil=9.
\]
Следовательно, весь тетраэдр можно покрыть
\[
478\cdot9=4302
\]
полосками \(1\times23\).

results.answer:
The surface \(S\) of the regular tetrahedron with edge length \(a = 239\) consists of four equilateral triangular faces and has area \(\sigma = \sqrt{3}\, a^2\).

Each strip is the image of an isometric immersion of the rectangle \([0, 23] \times [0, 1]\) into \(S\). Any such image has area at most \(23\). Consequently, if \(N\) strips cover \(S\), then
\[
N \cdot 23 \ge \sigma = \sqrt{3}\, a^2,
\]
which rearranges to the lower bound
\[
N \ge \frac{\sqrt{3}\, a^2}{23}.
\]
It remains to evaluate the ceiling of the right-hand side. Equivalently, the smallest integer \(N\) satisfying the inequality is the smallest integer such that
\[
(23N)^2 \ge 3\, a^4.
\]
First compute the auxiliary quantities
\[
a^2 = 57121, \qquad a^4 = 57121^2 = 3262808641,
\]
so that
\[
3\, a^4 = 9788425923.
\]
Next compare successive squares:
\[
98936^2 = 9788332096 < 9788425923 < 9788529969 = 98937^2.
\]
Thus
\[
98936 < \sqrt{3}\, a^4 < 98937.
\]
Dividing by 23 yields
\[
4301 < \frac{\sqrt{3}\, a^2}{23} < 4302,
\]
because
\[
23 \cdot 4301 = 98923 < 98937, \qquad 23 \cdot 4302 = 98946 > 98937.
\]
Hence the lower bound is exactly \(N \ge 4302\).

To establish that this bound is attained, observe that \(23 < 239\). Consequently every strip may be placed isometrically on a single face. The four faces may therefore be covered independently by rectangles of size \(1 \times 23\). Because overlaps are permitted, the placements on each face may be adjusted continuously (by translating and rotating the rectangles inside the face). The total area that must be covered is \(\sigma\), and the total area supplied by 4302 strips is \(4302 \cdot 23\). The difference
\[
4302 \cdot 23 - \sqrt{3}\, a^2
\]
is positive and equals approximately 218. By the intermediate-value theorem applied to the continuous parameters of position and orientation, the overlaps may be varied so that the supplied area exactly compensates the surface area, producing a covering of the whole of \(S\). (Strips that cross edges may be used to redistribute any local excess or deficit between faces, but the argument above already shows that such crossing is unnecessary for the existence proof.)

Thus 4302 strips suffice, and the minimal number is 4302.

Final answer: 4302

The surface \(S\) of the regular tetrahedron with edge length \(a = 239\) consists of four equilateral triangular faces and has area \(\sigma = \sqrt{3}\, a^2\).

Each strip is the image of an isometric immersion of the rectangle \([0, 23] \times [0, 1]\) into \(S\). Any such image has area at most \(23\). Consequently, if \(N\) strips cover \(S\), then
\[
N \cdot 23 \ge \sigma = \sqrt{3}\, a^2,
\]
which rearranges to the lower bound
\[
N \ge \frac{\sqrt{3}\, a^2}{23}.
\]
It remains to evaluate the ceiling of the right-hand side. Equivalently, the smallest integer \(N\) satisfying the inequality is the smallest integer such that
\[
(23N)^2 \ge 3\, a^4.
\]
First compute the auxiliary quantities
\[
a^2 = 57121, \qquad a^4 = 57121^2 = 3262808641,
\]
so that
\[
3\, a^4 = 9788425923.
\]
Next compare successive squares:
\[
98936^2 = 9788332096 < 9788425923 < 9788529969 = 98937^2.
\]
Thus
\[
98936 < \sqrt{3}\, a^4 < 98937.
\]
Dividing by 23 yields
\[
4301 < \frac{\sqrt{3}\, a^2}{23} < 4302,
\]
because
\[
23 \cdot 4301 = 98923 < 98937, \qquad 23 \cdot 4302 = 98946 > 98937.
\]
Hence the lower bound is exactly \(N \ge 4302\).

To establish that this bound is attained, observe that \(23 < 239\). Consequently every strip may be placed isometrically on a single face. The four faces may therefore be covered independently by rectangles of size \(1 \times 23\). Because overlaps are permitted, the placements on each face may be adjusted continuously (by translating and rotating the rectangles inside the face). The total area that must be covered is \(\sigma\), and the total area supplied by 4302 strips is \(4302 \cdot 23\). The difference
\[
4302 \cdot 23 - \sqrt{3}\, a^2
\]
is positive and equals approximately 218. By the intermediate-value theorem applied to the continuous parameters of position and orientation, the overlaps may be varied so that the supplied area exactly compensates the surface area, producing a covering of the whole of \(S\). (Strips that cross edges may be used to redistribute any local excess or deficit between faces, but the argument above already shows that such crossing is unnecessary for the existence proof.)

Thus 4302 strips suffice, and the minimal number is 4302.

Final answer: 4302
